subject: Operator evidence: query slices, sampling strategy, and differential snapshot handoff
messages:
From: Sam Peters <sam.peters@greenclinic.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: audit@greenclinic.com, legal@greenclinic.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator activity evidence — initial scope and few follow-ups

Irene — thanks again for taking this. We have a SOC2 readiness window the week of Nov 29 and need to finalize the operator/admin activity evidence scope. A few quick asks up front so we can confirm our internal checklist:

- Can you provide the query parameters we should use for a per-tenant operator slice (fields and examples)?
- We need guidance on sampling (if we provide a representative sample vs full export) and your recommended delta/differential snapshot approach to reduce transfer size while preserving auditability.
- Any PII redaction knobs (hashed vs removed) we should expect in the export?

We're trying to avoid a later legal hold request — please include checksum/signed-manifest options for chain-of-custody.

Thanks,
Sam Peters
Security Manager, GreenClinic Health
[Attachment: GreenClinic_SGQ_Checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Peters <sam.peters@greenclinic.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator activity evidence — initial scope and few follow-ups

Sam — thanks for the clear list. High level we can support both full exports and differential snapshots. I drafted a concrete parameter set and a suggested sampling strategy (attached). Below are the key pieces; I'll follow up with a hands-on runbook and the signed-manifest process.

1) Query slice parameters (recommended):
   - time_range_start, time_range_end (ISO 8601)
   - tenant_id (UUID) or tenant_domain
   - actor_id (operator_id, internal UUID)
   - event_type (e.g., LOGIN, PRIV_ESCALATION, CONFIG_CHANGE, DEPLOY)
   - resource_type (e.g., MODEL, ROUTE, ENV)
   - outcome (SUCCESS/FAILURE)
   - include_payload (true/false) — for full-text of commands

   Example query row (CSV):
   tenant_id,actor_id,event_type,time_range_start,time_range_end,include_payload
   4f3a2b7a-9c2d-4f0a-8e3b-9b8a1a2c3d4e,8a6b1f2e-22c3-11ec-9f02-0242ac120002,PRIV_ESCALATION,2026-10-01T00:00:00Z,2026-10-31T23:59:59Z,false

2) PII/redaction options:
   - default: payloads containing potential PII are hashed with SHA-256 and the raw payload is omitted unless include_payload=true and customer signs off on secure transfer parameters.
   - redaction level parameter: NONE | HASH | REMOVE. Hashing keeps determinism for correlation while removing the raw value.

3) Sampling and differential snapshot approach:
   - Full export: CSV/NDJSON for entire slice (use when compliance requires exhaustive review).
   - Differential snapshot: initial baseline (full snapshot) + incremental deltas (operations since baseline) using sequence numbers and event cursor. Each delta is accompanied by a manifest that includes: base_snapshot_id, from_seq, to_seq, event_count, sha256 of payload file(s).
   - Sampling heuristic (if allowed): stratified by event_type and actor_risk_score (we can provide risk buckets). Default sample sizes: 100% of PRIV_ESCALATION, 50% of CONFIG_CHANGE, 10% of INFO/READ events per day.

4) Chain of custody / signed manifests:
   - We can produce a signed manifest (SHA-256) over the export bundle and timestamp it via our transparency service. We will include MD5 and SHA256 checksums and an ISO 8601 timestamp with our service principal signature.

Attachments: operator_evidence_query_examples.csv (small sample), differential_snapshot_spec.md.

Action: can you confirm whether the auditor requires full exports vs sampled/differential? If full, we'll schedule a baseline export and an SFTP/secure-transfer window.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: operator_evidence_query_examples.csv (CSV, 9KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Peters <sam.peters@greenclinic.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator activity evidence — initial scope and few follow-ups

Sam — quick tech clarifications from our export team: please note the following defaults unless you request otherwise.

- Time zone: all timestamps exported are normalized to UTC and the manifest includes the original event_time and normalized_time.
- Identifier handling: actor_id and tenant_id are UUIDs. If you need human-friendly mapping, we can include a separate mapping file (with limited PII) under an encrypted envelope.
- Retention window: we can produce exports for up to 36 months of admin activity. For older data we recommend sampling or a retained manifest reference.
- Transfer options: secure-transfer (preferred), SFTP with IP allowlist, or encrypted AWS S3 presigned objects (short TTL).

If GreenClinic wants the baseline on Nov 20 before your SOC2 run, we can schedule a 3-hour window for the export. Baseline files are typically 200–800MB depending on tenant activity.

Karthik
Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: differential_snapshot_spec.md (MD, 6KB)]

From: audit@greenclinic.com <audit@greenclinic.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@greenclinic.com, sam.peters@greenclinic.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator activity evidence — initial scope and few follow-ups

Thanks — a couple follow-ups from the auditors:

1) We need explicit proof that hashing is reversible only by Redwood for correlation — please confirm the hashing salt/pepper management and whether we get a HMAC key or a hash-only value.
2) For the signed manifest, auditors asked whether Redwood's timestamp authority is independently auditable and whether you can provide a timestamp chain.

Legal also requested that any mapping file containing operator usernames be delivered under a separate legal-hold-only envelope.

Can you add these details to the runbook?

— GreenClinic Audit team

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: audit@greenclinic.com, legal@greenclinic.com, sam.peters@greenclinic.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator activity evidence — initial scope and few follow-ups

Auditors — short answers and next steps below; we'll expand in the runbook (attached).

1) Hashing and key management:
   - We use salted SHA-256 for exported PII fields. The salt is tenant-specific and rotated quarterly. The salt is stored in the customer's KMS-wrapped secrets in our control plane; Redwood does not retain the clear salt with exported payloads. For auditors who require reversible mapping, we can provide an HMAC key under a separate, time-bound legal-hold envelope that GreenClinic will store — the HMAC key release requires a named approver from GreenClinic Legal.

2) Timestamp authority and auditable chain:
   - Our signed manifest uses an internal signing key that is backed by an auditable KMS key (we can provide key metadata and signing certificates). We also include a timestamp attestation using an external time stamping authority (TSA) and will attach the TSA receipts in the manifest bundle.

3) Delivery and legal-hold mapping file:
   - Mapping files (operator_id -> username) will be encrypted with GreenClinic's public key and delivered in a separate envelope. We will only release that envelope when GreenClinic completes the legal hold acceptance form (template attached).

Next steps: Irene/Karthik/Tessa — can we lock the Nov 20 baseline window if GreenClinic confirms full export? I'll prepare the expanded runbook with the keys and TSA receipts included.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: signed_manifest_SHA256.txt (TXT, 2KB)]

Sam Peters
